topics.title: AccuRanker
topics.description: AccuRanker is a rank tracking tool built specifically for speed and accuracy at scale, commonly used by agencies and larger sites that need to track rankings for a large number of keywords.

topics.title: Agentic Search
topics.description: Agentic search is when an AI system does not just answer a question, but takes actions on a user's behalf, such as browsing multiple pages, comparing options, or completing a task like booking or purchasing. It represents a shift from search as information retrieval toward search as a component of autonomous task completion.

topics.title: Ahrefs Brand Radar
topics.description: Ahrefs Brand Radar is a feature that tracks how often and how prominently a brand appears within AI-generated answers, extending Ahrefs' existing tracking capabilities from traditional search into AI visibility.

topics.title: Ahrefs
topics.description: Ahrefs is an all-in-one software suite that provides data on backlinks, keyword rankings, and website performance. It works by crawling the web to map out how pages connect to one another, allowing users to analyze their own site’s link profile or research the backlink strategies of competitors. The platform offers a variety of tools to identify broken links, monitor new link acquisition, and discover opportunities for outreach to improve overall site visibility.

topics.title: Ahrefs
topics.description: Ahrefs is an SEO platform widely used for backlink analysis, keyword research, and rank tracking. It maintains one of the largest independent indexes of backlinks on the web, making it a common choice specifically for link-building research.
resources: The Official Ahrefs Tutorial: How to Use Ahrefs to Improve SEO

topics.title: AI Chat Prompts
topics.description: AI chat prompts are the actual questions and phrasings people type into AI assistants like ChatGPT when looking for information. Studying these gives insight into how people phrase requests conversationally, which often differs from how they type short keyword searches into a traditional search engine.
resources: How to do prompt research for AI SEO
AI Search Prompts: How to Turn SEO Keywords Into Buyer Questions
How to Optimize for Google AI Overviews: What Businesses Should Do Now

topics.title: AI Overviews
topics.description: AI Overviews are AI-generated summaries that Google shows directly at the top of search results, answering a query before the user scrolls down to individual links. They are built using retrieval from indexed web content, so being cited depends on many of the same technical and content factors as ranking well in normal search results.
resources: AI Overviews: What Are They & How to Optimize for Them
Google AI Overviews & SEO: What's gonna change?
Google Just Expanded AI Overviews: This Is What Still Gets Clicked

topics.title: AI Tools for Content
topics.description: AI tools for content are software platforms that analyze top-ranking content for a given topic and suggest what a piece of writing is missing, such as related subtopics, terms, or depth of coverage.

topics.title: AI Visibility Measurement
topics.description: AI visibility measurement is the set of metrics used to track how visible a brand is inside AI-generated answers, covering how often it appears across a set of representative prompts, how often and how prominently it gets cited, how it compares to competitors, and whether it is associated with positive or neutral sentiment.

topics.title: Algorithm Updates
topics.description: Algorithm updates are changes search engines make to how they evaluate and rank content, which can shift rankings across the web without any specific site being penalized individually. They range from broad core updates affecting many sites, to updates specifically targeting spam or low-quality content patterns.
resources: What Are Algorithm Updates in SEO?
How to Recover From Any Google Algorithm Update (And Protect Your Site From Future Updates)

topics.title: Article, FAQ & HowTo Schema
topics.description: Article schema marks up a piece of content as a news article or blog post, with structured details like publish date and author. FAQ schema marks up a list of questions and answers, sometimes allowing them to display directly in search results. HowTo schema marks up step-by-step instructions, structuring each step so it can potentially be shown directly in search results.

topics.title: Attributes & Relationships
topics.description: Attributes are facts a system tracks about a specific entity, such as a company's founding year or industry. Relationships describe how entities connect to each other, such as a person founding a particular company. Together they let a system answer questions that require connecting information across multiple sources, not just retrieving one page.

topics.title: Author & Organization Consistency
topics.description: This is making sure the name, biography, and stated facts about an author or organization match wherever they appear, whether on the company's own site, a guest post, or a professional profile. Inconsistent details, such as different job titles or misspelled names, make it harder for a system to confirm it is looking at the same entity.

topics.title: Authors & Brands
topics.description: This refers to schema and structured data specifically identifying the author of a piece of content or the brand behind a product or business. Clearly marking authorship and brand ownership supports both credibility signals and entity recognition across the web.

topics.title: Backlinks & Anchor Text
topics.description: A backlink is a link from one website pointing to another, treated by search engines as a signal of trust or endorsement. Anchor text is the clickable, visible text of that link, and its wording gives search engines additional context about what the linked page is about.
resources: What are backlinks in SEO & how do I get them?
About Anchor Texts in Backlink Audit
Backlinks for SEO: Complete Guide for 2026
Anchor Text: How I Optimize it (Step-by-Step)

topics.title: Before/After Prompt Tests
topics.description: This means running the same set of AI prompts before and after making a change to a website, then comparing the answers to see whether the change actually affected how AI systems describe or cite the brand.

topics.title: Bingbot
topics.description: Bingbot is the web crawler used by Microsoft's Bing search engine to discover and index web pages. It also supplies some of the underlying data used by other services built on Bing's index, so a page invisible to Bingbot can lose visibility beyond Bing itself.

topics.title: Branded vs Non-Branded
topics.description: Branded queries are searches that include a company's name, such as "Nike running shoes," while non-branded queries are generic searches without it, such as "best running shoes." Tracking the split between the two shows whether traffic is coming mostly from people who already know the brand or from people discovering it for the first time.

topics.title: Breadcrumb Rich Result
topics.description: A breadcrumb rich result is when the navigational path of a page, such as Home > Blog > Article, displays directly within its search result listing instead of the full URL. It is enabled through breadcrumb schema markup and gives searchers a clearer sense of where a page sits within a site.

topics.title: Breadcrumb, Video & Review Schema
topics.description: Breadcrumb schema marks up the navigational path shown above a page's title, such as Home > Category > Product. Video schema provides structured details about an embedded video, like its duration and thumbnail. Review schema marks up ratings and reviews, which can enable star ratings to appear directly in search results.

topics.title: BrightLocal
topics.description: BrightLocal is a local SEO platform used for tracking local rankings, auditing citation consistency, and managing reviews across multiple business locations.

topics.title: BuzzStream
topics.description: BuzzStream is an outreach and relationship management tool used in link building and digital PR, helping practitioners track contacts, send pitches, and manage ongoing outreach campaigns at scale.

topics.title: Canonical
topics.description: A canonical tag is a snippet of HTML code that tells search engines which version of a webpage is the primary or "master" version. When multiple pages on a website contain identical or very similar content, this tag prevents confusion by signaling to crawlers that they should treat these pages as one. This consolidates ranking signals and ensures your preferred page appears in search results.
resources: Canonical URLs: SEO Best Practices, Common Issues, and How to Fix Them
What is a Canonical Tag? (SEO Basic Explained)

topics.title: Canonicalization
topics.description: Canonicalization is the process of telling search engines which URL is the official version of a page when the same content is reachable through more than one URL, such as with or without a tracking parameter. Without this, a search engine might treat duplicate versions of a page as separate, unrelated pages and split ranking signals between them.
resources: Canonical URLs: How Does Google Pick the One?
What is a Canonical Tag? (SEO Basic Explained)

topics.title: Case Studies & Benchmarks
topics.description: Case studies and benchmarks provide evidence-based insights by analyzing specific project outcomes and industry performance standards. A case study highlights the journey, challenges, and results of a particular initiative, while a benchmark compares performance metrics against established averages or competitor data. Together, they act as objective resources that illustrate what is possible and provide a clear baseline for evaluating success within a given field.
resources: How to Build a Killer SEO Case Study
Six reasons why case studies are crucial for digital marketing success

topics.title: ccTLD vs Subfolder vs Subdomain
topics.description: A ccTLD is a country-specific domain ending, like .de for Germany, giving the strongest signal of geographic targeting but requiring separate domains for each market. A subfolder keeps international content under one main domain, such as [example.com/de/](http://example.com/de/), while a subdomain places it on a separate address like [de.example.com](http://de.example.com). Each approach involves different tradeoffs between geographic targeting strength and shared domain authority.

topics.title: Chat-Based Search
topics.description: Chat-based search is when someone finds information by asking a conversational AI assistant, such as ChatGPT or Claude, instead of typing a query into a traditional search engine. The assistant may retrieve information from the web, its training data, or both, then respond in natural language rather than showing a results page.
resources: What is the difference between conversational AI search and a chatbot?
The Future of Search: Generative AI and Chat-Based Search
How Web Search Inside AI Chatbots Works

topics.title: ChatGPT Search
topics.description: ChatGPT Search is a feature that lets ChatGPT retrieve current information from the web when answering a question, rather than relying only on its training data. It presents a conversational answer along with linked sources, similar in concept to a dedicated answer engine.

topics.title: Chunking
topics.description: Chunking is the process of splitting a long document into smaller pieces before it gets indexed for retrieval. Systems typically search and retrieve at the chunk level rather than the whole-document level, since a smaller, focused piece of text is easier to match accurately to a specific question. How a document gets chunked can affect whether the right piece of information gets found and cited.

topics.title: Citation Flow
topics.description: Citation Flow is a metric from Majestic that estimates the raw link popularity of a website, based on how many sites link to it regardless of their quality. It is typically compared alongside Trust Flow, since a large gap between the two can indicate a site has many low-quality links.

topics.title: Citation Rate & Position
topics.description: Citation rate is how often an AI system cites a particular source when generating an answer. Citation position refers to how prominently that source appears within the citations, since being the first source listed generally carries more visibility and credibility than being buried further down.

topics.title: Citation Sources
topics.description: Citation sources are the specific websites and platforms that AI systems most frequently pull from and cite when generating answers, such as community forums, encyclopedic sites, and video platforms. Understanding which sources get cited most often helps prioritize where a brand should have a genuine, active presence.

topics.title: ClaudeBot
topics.description: ClaudeBot is a web crawler operated by Anthropic that browses the internet to collect data for training and improving its artificial intelligence models. It visits websites to read and process content, which allows Claude AI to understand and respond to user queries with updated information. Website owners can manage how this bot interacts with their pages by using standard directives in their robots.txt file.
resources: What is ClaudeBot? (The Web Crawler Behind Claude AI)

topics.title: Clearscope
topics.description: Clearscope is a content optimization tool that grades a piece of writing against top-performing content for a given topic, suggesting relevant terms and concepts that may be missing.

topics.title: Cloaking & Doorways
topics.description: Cloaking is showing search engines different content than what a real visitor sees, typically to manipulate rankings while displaying something else to users. Doorway pages are low-value pages created specifically to rank for narrow search terms and funnel visitors elsewhere, rather than serving as genuine destinations. Both are explicitly against search engine guidelines.
resources: What is cloaking in SEO? | Black Hat SEO Technique Explained
Doorway Pages vs. Programmatic SEO: How to Avoid a Google Penalty

topics.title: Community Presence
topics.description: Community presence is a brand or individual's activity and reputation within online communities such as Reddit, Quora, and niche forums, where people ask questions and share opinions candidly. These communities are increasingly pulled from directly by AI systems when forming answers, making genuine presence there valuable beyond traditional SEO value.

topics.title: Competitive Answer Share
topics.description: Competitive answer share measures a brand's presence in AI-generated answers relative to its competitors, across the same set of prompts. It shows whether a brand is winning, losing, or roughly matching its competitors for visibility inside AI systems.

topics.title: Competitor Benchmarking
topics.description: Competitor benchmarking is the practice of comparing a website's search and AI visibility performance directly against competitors, rather than only tracking its own metrics in isolation. It gives context for whether a given number is actually good or bad within the competitive landscape.

topics.title: Competitor Gap Analysis
topics.description: Competitor gap analysis is the process of identifying the topics, keywords, and content formats that your competitors are ranking for but your website is not. By comparing your existing content against the top-performing pages in your industry, you can pinpoint specific areas where your site is missing information or failing to address user intent. This practice helps you discover untapped opportunities to create more comprehensive resources and capture traffic that currently flows to other sites.
resources: 5 Key Components Of A Competitive Gap Analysis
What Is Content Gap Analysis in SEO? (Explained in 2 Minutes!)

topics.title: Content & Schema A/B Tests
topics.description: This is testing two versions of a page's content or structured data against each other to see which one performs better in search or AI visibility, rather than assuming a change is an improvement without checking.

topics.title: Content Consolidation
topics.description: Content consolidation is the process of combining multiple low-performing or redundant pages on a website into a single, comprehensive piece of content. By merging similar topics, you reduce keyword cannibalization and create a more authoritative resource that provides greater value to readers. This practice involves redirecting the old, individual URLs to the new, unified page, which helps streamline your site structure and improves the overall relevance of your information.

topics.title: Content Freshness & Decay
topics.description: Content freshness is whether a piece of content still reads as current and up to date, which search and AI systems weigh when a query specifically benefits from recent information. Content decay is the gradual decline in a page's rankings and traffic over time as it ages or as competing content improves, requiring an ongoing process of auditing, updating, or consolidating older content to keep it performing.

topics.title: Content Lifecycle
topics.description: The content lifecycle covers everything that happens to a piece of content after it is first published, including planning its production, monitoring how it performs over time, deciding whether to refresh, rewrite, merge, or remove it, and formally deindexing pages that no longer serve a purpose.

topics.title: Cloudflare Controls & Pay-Per-Crawl
topics.description: Cloudflare offers tools that let website owners manage how AI crawlers access their content at the network level, including the ability to block known AI bots by default. Pay-per-crawl is a newer model where a site can charge AI companies for the right to crawl its content, rather than allowing free access or blocking it entirely.
resources: The crawl-to-click gap: Cloudflare data on AI bots, training, and referrals

topics.title: Copilot & Gemini
topics.description: Copilot is Microsoft's AI assistant, integrated into Bing search and other Microsoft products, capable of retrieving web information to answer questions. Gemini is Google's AI assistant, offering similar conversational and retrieval capabilities as a separate product from Google's main search engine.

topics.title: Core Updates
topics.description: A core update is a broad change to a search engine's overall ranking systems, intended to improve results generally rather than target a specific type of content or violation. Core updates can cause noticeable ranking shifts across many sites, and there is often no single fix beyond genuinely improving content quality and relevance over time.
resources: Google Search's core updates and your website

topics.title: Core Web Vitals
topics.description: Core Web Vitals are a specific set of metrics Google uses to measure user experience, covering how fast a page becomes visually complete, how quickly it responds to interaction, and how much its layout shifts while loading. They are used as one of many signals in Google's ranking system, and slow or unstable pages tend to perform worse both with users and in rankings.
resources: Understanding Core Web Vitals and Google search results
Core Web Vitals: What They Are & How to Improve Them
Google Core Web Vitals: A Complete Guide For Beginners
What are Core Web Vitals? | Core Web Vitals explained in 7 minutes

topics.title: Crawl Budget
topics.description: Crawl budget is the amount of crawling capacity a search engine allocates to a given website within a certain time period. Large or poorly structured sites can burn through crawl budget on unimportant pages, leaving important pages crawled less often or not at all. Managing crawl budget mostly means removing waste, such as duplicate URLs or low-value pages, so crawlers spend their time on pages that matter.
resources: Crawl Budget: What Is It and Why Is It Important for SEO?
What is Crawl Budget in SEO | How to do Crawl Budget Optimization
Crawl Budget and the Crawl Stats report - Google Search Console Training

topics.title: Crawling & Indexing
topics.description: Crawling is the process of a bot visiting pages on a website to read their content. Indexing is what happens after crawling, when a search engine stores and organizes that content so it can be retrieved later for relevant searches. A page can be crawled without being indexed, for example if it is judged low quality or duplicate.
resources: What is Crawling and Indexing in SEO?
Crawling & Indexing: How the Google Index Works
Crawling, Indexing and Ranking | SEO for Beginners

topics.title: Crawling, Indexing, and Ranking
topics.description: Search engines function by using automated programs called spiders or crawlers to scan the internet, discover web pages, and follow links from one site to another. Once these pages are found, the information is processed and stored in a massive database known as an index, where it is categorized based on content and relevance. When a user performs a search, the engine retrieves the most suitable results from this index and orders them according to complex algorithms that determine which pages best answer the user's query.
resources: Website Crawling, Indexing, and Ranking Explained
SEO Basics: Crawling, Indexing, and Ranking

topics.title: Custom Charts & Images
topics.description: Custom charts and images are visuals created specifically for a piece of content, using original data rather than generic stock graphics. They give search and AI systems a unique visual asset tied to that content, rather than an image that could be found anywhere else.
resources: How Images Affect SEO: Can Adding a Diagram Really Drive Rankings?
How custom visuals boosted organic traffic by up to 110%

topics.title: Data-Driven PR
topics.description: Data-driven PR is a specific digital PR tactic where a brand runs original research or a survey, then pitches journalists the resulting statistics as the basis for a story. It gives journalists something concrete and citable to write about, increasing the odds of coverage compared to a generic pitch.

topics.title: Data Tables
topics.description: Data tables present information in rows and columns rather than paragraphs of prose. They are easier for both humans scanning quickly and AI systems extracting specific facts to parse accurately, since the structure clearly separates individual data points.

topics.title: Dense Retrieval
topics.description: Dense retrieval is a method of finding relevant documents using embeddings and vector similarity, rather than matching exact keywords. It compares the numerical representation of a query against the numerical representations of stored content to find the closest matches by meaning. It is the retrieval method most closely associated with semantic and vector search.
resources: Top 3 RAG Retrieval Strategies: Sparse, Dense, & Hybrid Explained

topics.title: Digital PR
topics.description: Digital PR is the practice of earning media coverage and links from real publications by pitching journalists newsworthy stories, data, or angles, rather than directly requesting a link.

topics.title: Direct Answers
topics.description: A direct answer is a plainly stated response to a specific question, placed clearly in the content rather than buried inside a long explanation. Content written this way is more likely to be pulled out and used by featured snippets, AI Overviews, and other answer systems.

topics.title: Directories & Databases
topics.description: Directories and databases are external listings of a business or brand, such as industry directories or structured data sources. They act as independent confirmations of a brand's existence and details, beyond what the brand claims about itself on its own website.

topics.title: Disambiguation & Salience
topics.description: Disambiguation is the process a system uses to determine which specific entity a piece of content refers to when multiple entities share a similar name, such as two different people named Michael Jordan. Salience describes how central an entity is within a given piece of content, distinguishing a page that is genuinely about that entity from one that only mentions it in passing.

topics.title: Domain & Protocol Changes
topics.description: A domain change is moving a website to an entirely new domain name. A protocol change is switching between HTTP and HTTPS, or between www and non-www versions of a URL. Both require careful redirect handling so search engines and users are correctly sent to the new location.
resources: Domain and DNS Migration Checklist When Changing Hosting Provider
Domain Migration Made Simple: A Step-by-Step Guide
How To Transfer Domain? | Easy step-by-step guide
Why Your Data Infrastructure Migration Project Will Fail (And How to Succeed)

topics.title: Domain Authority
topics.description: Domain Authority is a score developed by Moz that estimates how likely an entire website is to rank in search results, based largely on the quantity and quality of links pointing to it. It is measured on a relative scale and is most useful for comparing one site against another, rather than as an absolute number.

topics.title: Duplicate Content
topics.description: Duplicate content is when the same or nearly identical content exists across multiple pages, either on the same site or across different sites. It confuses ranking systems about which version should be shown, and can dilute the ranking signals that would otherwise concentrate on a single strong page.

topics.title: Ecommerce SEO
topics.description: Ecommerce SEO is the practice of optimizing an online store's product and category pages so they rank well in search, addressing challenges specific to retail sites like large product catalogs and complex filtering systems.

topics.title: E-E-A-T
topics.description: E-E-A-T stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness. It is a framework Google uses to judge the quality and credibility of content and its creator, rather than a direct, measurable ranking factor. AI systems increasingly use similar signals when deciding which sources to trust and cite.
resources: Our latest update to the quality rater guidelines: E-A-T gets an extra E for Experience
Google E-E-A-T: What it is & how it affects SEO
What is Google E-E-A-T (plus tools to improve yours)

topics.title: Embeddings
topics.description: Embeddings are numerical representations of text that capture its meaning, allowing a computer to compare how similar two pieces of text are. Words or sentences with related meanings end up close together in this numerical space, even if they share no common words. Search and AI systems use embeddings to power semantic and vector search.

topics.title: Entities vs Keywords
topics.description: A keyword is a string of text, such as "Nike shoes." An entity is the actual, specific thing behind it, such as Nike as a distinct company with a history and headquarters. Search and AI systems have moved from matching keyword strings toward understanding which entity a piece of content is actually about.

topics.title: Entity & Sentiment
topics.description: This tracks whether an AI system correctly associates a brand with the right topics and entities, and whether that association carries positive, neutral, or negative sentiment. A brand can be frequently mentioned by an AI system while still being associated with the wrong context or an unfavorable tone.

topics.title: Entity Consistency
topics.description: Entity consistency is how uniformly a brand or person's identity appears across the web, including directories, social profiles, and mentions that are not directly controlled by that brand. Search and AI systems use this consistency to confirm that scattered mentions across the internet all refer to the same real entity, rather than several unrelated ones.

topics.title: Entity SEO
topics.description: Entity SEO is the practice of optimizing for how search and AI systems understand specific, distinct real-world things, such as a person, company, or product, rather than just matching strings of text. It focuses on making sure a system can correctly identify what an entity is, how it relates to other entities, and whether different mentions across the web refer to the same one.

topics.title: Expired Domain Abuse
topics.description: Expired domain abuse is buying a domain that previously had an established reputation and history, then repurposing it with unrelated content purely to exploit its existing authority and rankings. Search engines treat this as manipulative because the new content has no real connection to what earned that domain its original trust.
resources: Expired Domains: What Still Works, What's Spam, and How to Rebuild Safely
How I Find Expired Domains with Backlink Goldmines (and When They’re Worth It)

topics.title: Faceted Navigation
topics.description: Faceted navigation refers to filter and sort options on a website, such as filtering products by size or color, that can generate a huge number of similar or duplicate URLs. Without careful control, this can flood a crawler with near-identical pages and waste crawl budget on variations that add little unique value.
resources: Managing crawling of faceted navigation URLs
Faceted Navigation: Definition, Examples & SEO Best Practices
Faceted Navigation | PRG | Lesson 12/34 | Semrush Academy

topics.title: Featured Snippets
topics.description: A featured snippet is a highlighted answer box that sometimes appears at the very top of Google's search results, pulled directly from a page further down the results list. Winning a featured snippet often means writing a clear, direct answer near the top of a page in a format, like a short paragraph or list, that Google can extract cleanly.

topics.title: Folders & URL Structure
topics.description: This is the organization of a website's URLs into logical folders that reflect the site's content hierarchy, such as grouping all blog posts under /blog/ and all products under /products/. Clear, readable URLs help both users and crawlers understand what a page is about before they even load it.
resources: 10 Essentials To Create The Most Effective SEO URL Structure
URL structure best practices for Google Search
HTML & CSS for Beginners: File Structure
The Perfect URL Structure for SEO!

topics.title: Content Formatting & Readability
topics.description: Content formatting and readability covers how a piece of writing is structured for easy scanning and comprehension, including paragraph length, use of bullet points, and sentence complexity. Content that is easy to read tends to keep visitors engaged longer and is easier for both users and AI systems to extract information from.
resources: The Power of Formatting: How Formatting Text Boosts SEO
How Does Blog Formatting Improve Content SEO in 2026?
How Much Does Readability Affect SEO?
How Readability Affects SEO: 10 Critical Factors That Rank Your Site

topics.title: Forums & Communities
topics.description: Forums and communities, such as Reddit and Quora, are places where people ask questions and discuss topics in their own words, often more candidly than in polished articles. They are a valuable source of real questions and language for content research, and are increasingly pulled from directly by AI systems when forming answers.

topics.title: Frase
topics.description: Frase is a content optimization tool that combines keyword research, content briefs, and AI-assisted writing suggestions, helping writers structure content to match what is already ranking well for a target topic.

topics.title: GEO & SEO Testing
topics.description: This is the practice of running structured experiments to check whether a change actually improved visibility, rather than assuming it did. It includes testing content or schema changes, comparing AI-generated answers before and after a change, and benchmarking performance against competitors.

topics.title: Geo-Targeting & Localization
topics.description: Geo-targeting is signaling to search engines which country or region a page is intended for, while localization is adapting the page itself for that audience, including language, currency, spelling, and units. Signals such as hreflang annotations, a country-specific domain or URL structure, and genuinely localized content help search engines serve the right version of a page to the right users.
resources: Geo-Targeting SEO: A Game-Changer for Local Businesses

topics.title: Google AI Mode
topics.description: Google AI Mode is a search experience that generates a conversational, AI-written response to a query, going further than a standard AI Overview by allowing follow-up questions within the same session. It draws on retrieved web content, meaning visibility here depends on many of the same technical and content factors as ranking in standard search results.

topics.title: Google Analytics
topics.description: Google Analytics is a free web analytics platform that tracks website traffic, including where visitors come from, which pages they view, and whether they complete meaningful actions like purchases or sign-ups.

topics.title: Google Business Profile
topics.description: Google Business Profile is a free listing that shows a business's hours, photos, phone number, and reviews directly in Google Maps and local search results. It is typically the single most important asset for any business trying to appear in local search.

topics.title: Google Data Studio
topics.description: Google Data Studio, now known as Looker Studio, is a free tool for building custom dashboards and reports by pulling data from sources like Google Analytics and Search Console into a single visual interface.

topics.title: Google Discover
topics.description: Google Discover is a personalized content feed shown on mobile devices, surfacing articles based on a user's interests rather than a specific search query. Appearing in Discover depends on factors like content quality and image optimization, but there is no way to directly target it the way you can target a specific keyword.

topics.title: Google-Extended
topics.description: Google-Extended is a specific crawler control that lets a website choose whether Google can use its content to train Gemini and improve AI features like AI Overviews, separately from whether the site allows normal Googlebot crawling for search. Blocking it does not affect a site's regular search rankings, but can affect its visibility inside Google's AI-generated answers.
resources: Overview of Google crawlers and fetchers (user agents)
Google-Extended: What It Does and Should You Block It?

topics.title: Google Keyword Planner
topics.description: Google Keyword Planner is a free tool, originally built for Google Ads, that shows search volume estimates and keyword suggestions based on Google's own search data. It is often used as a baseline data source alongside paid third-party keyword tools.
resources: How to Use Google Keyword Planner
How to Use Google Keyword Planner for SEO (It's FREE!)
How to Use Google Keyword Planner (How the Top 1% Find Profitable Keywords)

topics.title: Google Search Console
topics.description: Google Search Console is a free tool from Google that shows exactly how a website performs in Google's own search results, including which queries it appears for, click-through rates, indexing errors, and manual penalties.

topics.title: Googlebot
topics.description: Googlebot is the web crawler Google uses to discover and read pages across the internet, feeding the content it finds into Google's search index. It renders JavaScript reasonably well compared to most other crawlers, though heavy or slow-loading scripts can still cause parts of a page to be missed.
resources: Googlebot: What it is, how it works & how to optimize

topics.title: GPTBot
topics.description: GPTBot is the crawler operated by OpenAI, used to gather web content for training AI models. A website can block it entirely through robots.txt if it does not want its content used for that purpose, though doing so may also reduce visibility in tools that rely on GPTBot for retrieval.
resources: What Is GPTBot, and Should You Block It?
GPTBot: What Is It and How Does It Crawl Websites?

topics.title: GSC API & BigQuery Export
topics.description: The Google Search Console API allows programmatic access to search performance data, rather than only viewing it through the web interface. The BigQuery export sends this data automatically into Google's BigQuery platform, enabling larger scale analysis and longer data retention than Search Console's standard interface allows.

topics.title: Heading Structure
topics.description: Heading structure refers to how a page uses heading tags, from a single main heading down through subheadings, to organize content into a logical hierarchy. A clear heading structure helps both readers scan content quickly and helps search engines understand how a page's sections relate to each other.
resources: What Are Heading Tags? & Why They're Important for SEO
How to Use H1 H2 H3 Tags for SEO

topics.title: Helpful Content System
topics.description: The Helpful Content System is a part of Google's ranking systems designed to reward content created primarily to help people, and demote content created primarily to rank in search engines. It evaluates signals like whether content demonstrates real experience and whether it exists mainly to attract search traffic rather than serve a genuine audience need.
resources: Here’s What Google Classifies as Helpful Content

topics.title: How Agents Browse
topics.description: This covers the technical process by which an AI agent navigates websites autonomously, including how it reads page content, follows links, and interprets forms or buttons to complete a task, generally without a human directing each individual step.

topics.title: How AI is Changing SEO
topics.description: AI systems are changing how people find information, moving some search behavior away from typing keywords into a search bar and toward asking questions directly to a chat interface. This shift means content now needs to work for two audiences: traditional search crawlers and AI systems that retrieve and summarize information. The technical mechanics behind this shift, such as how AI models process and retrieve text, are covered in more depth in the AI Engineer roadmap.

topics.title: How Search Engines Work
topics.description: Search engines function as massive indexing systems that constantly crawl the internet to discover, analyze, and store web content. They use automated software bots, often called spiders or crawlers, to follow links from page to page, gathering information to add to their vast databases. Once this data is collected, complex algorithms evaluate the content based on various factors to determine its relevance and quality, ultimately organizing it so that the most helpful results can be retrieved instantly when a user enters a search query.
resources: In-depth guide to how Google Search works
How Google and Search Engines Work

topics.title: Hreflang
topics.description: Hreflang is an HTML attribute that tells search engines which language and regional version of a page to show to users based on their location and language settings. It prevents search engines from showing the wrong language version, or treating translated versions of the same page as duplicate content.

topics.title: HTTP & Status Codes
topics.description: HTTP status codes are three-digit codes a server sends back describing what happened with a request, such as whether a page loaded successfully, moved, or failed to load. Understanding these codes is essential for diagnosing why a page might not be getting crawled, indexed, or displayed correctly.
resources: HTTP Status Codes Explained In 5 Minutes

topics.title: HTTPS & Security
topics.description: HTTPS is a secure, encrypted version of the standard web protocol, shown to users as a padlock icon in the browser address bar. It is treated as a baseline trust signal by search engines rather than a major ranking factor on its own, and its absence can actively hurt user trust and conversion rates.
resources: HTTPS & Site Security for SEO: Everything You Must Know in 2026
HTTPS and SEO: How Website Security Impacts Your Rankings

topics.title: Hybrid Search
topics.description: Hybrid search combines lexical and vector search in a single system, so it can catch exact matches, like product names or error codes, while also catching content that means the same thing but uses different words. This combination generally performs better than either method alone, since lexical search alone misses paraphrased content and vector search alone misses exact terms.
resources: The Complete Guide to Hybrid Search in RAG

topics.title: Image & Video Packs
topics.description: An image pack or video pack is a horizontal row of image or video thumbnails shown within search results for queries where visual content is especially relevant. Appearing in these packs depends on proper image or video optimization and relevant structured data.

topics.title: Image Optimisation
topics.description: Image optimisation is the practice of preparing images so they load quickly and remain accessible and understandable to both users and search engines, covering how images are described, named, compressed, and formatted.
resources: Image SEO: How to Optimize Images for Search Engines & Users
How To Write Great Image Alt Text And Get More SEO Traffic

topics.title: Impressions, Clicks & CTR
topics.description: Impressions are how often a page appears in search results for a query, whether or not anyone clicks it. Clicks are how many people actually click through. CTR, or click-through rate, is the percentage of impressions that turn into clicks, and a low CTR relative to ranking position can signal that a title or description is not compelling enough.

topics.title: Index Coverage & Index Bloat
topics.description: Index coverage refers to how much of a website's content is actually included in a search engine's index versus excluded for various reasons. Index bloat is when a large number of low-value, thin, or duplicate pages get indexed, diluting a site's overall quality signals and making it harder for a search engine to focus on the pages that matter.
resources: Index bloat in SEO: What it is & how to fix it
What Is Index Bloat in SEO? (And How To Fix It)
How To Understand How Google Indexes Your Website
Why You Must Pay Attention To Index Bloat

topics.title: Influencer Outreach
topics.description: Influencer outreach is the practice of getting individual creators, bloggers, or influencers to mention, review, or link to a brand. It works similarly to digital PR but targets individual voices with their own audiences, rather than publications.

topics.title: Information Gain
topics.description: Information gain is whether a piece of content adds something genuinely new, such as a fact, data point, or perspective, compared to what already exists in top search results. Content that only restates what is already widely available offers little reason for a search or AI system to prefer it over existing sources.
resources: What Is Information Gain in SEO? (and How To Add It to Your Content)
Information Gain In SEO (This Is How You Beat AI Content)

topics.title: Internal Anchor Text
topics.description: Internal anchor text is the clickable, visible text used for links pointing between pages on the same website. Descriptive anchor text gives search engines additional context about the linked page's topic, while vague text like "click here" provides no useful signal.
resources: What Is Anchor Text? An Overview + Best Practices
Anchor Text: How I Optimize it (Step-by-Step)

topics.title: Internal Linking
topics.description: Internal linking is the practice of linking between pages on the same website. It helps crawlers discover new pages, distributes ranking authority across a site, and signals which pages are related to each other. A page that receives many internal links is generally treated as more important than one that receives none.
resources: The ultimate guide to internal linking for SEO
How to use internal linking for SEO
How to use Internal Links to Boost Google Rankings

topics.title: International SEO
topics.description: International SEO is the practice of optimizing a website to serve and rank well for audiences in multiple countries or languages, addressing how content, URLs, and targeting signals differ across markets.

topics.title: Introduction
topics.description: Search is no longer just about ranking in a list of blue links. People now find answers through Google's AI Overviews, chat assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, and voice-based answer engines, alongside traditional search results. This roadmap covers SEO, GEO, and AEO as three connected layers of the same discipline: getting found, getting cited, and getting your content pulled into a direct answer. It walks through technical foundations, content strategy, entity and authority signals, and measurement, so you can build visibility across both classic search engines and the AI systems now sitting alongside them.
resources: What Is SEO and Why is it Important?
The Complete SEO & AI SEO Course for 2026 (Full Beginner’s Guide)

topics.title: Keyword Placement & Over-Optimisation
topics.description: Keyword placement is where and how often target keywords appear within a page's content. Over-optimisation is repeating a keyword unnaturally often in an attempt to manipulate rankings, which can make content read awkwardly and may trigger a quality penalty rather than helping visibility.
resources: The Ultimate Guide to Keyword Placement for SEO
Keyword Placement Strategies: How to Use Keywords Effectively for SEO
How to Use Keywords in Your Content for SEO (The RIGHT Way!)
Where to Put Keywords on Your Website (for SEO & AI)

topics.title: Keyword Research
topics.description: Keyword research is the process of finding the actual words and phrases people use when searching for something related to a topic. It typically involves checking search volume, competition, and related terms to decide which topics are worth targeting with content.
resources: How to Do Keyword Research for SEO (Start to Finish)
Keyword Research for SEO in 2026: Step-by-Step Tutorial
Primary Keywords: The Most Critical Part of Your SEO Strategy?
Keyword Research Tutorial for Google and AI SEO

topics.title: Knowledge Graphs
topics.description: A knowledge graph is a database that stores entities and the relationships between them, used by search and AI systems to understand and connect real-world information. Google maintains its own, and Wikidata is a large, open, publicly editable one that many systems reference. Being accurately represented in these graphs helps a brand or person get correctly recognized across different platforms.

topics.title: Knowledge Panels
topics.description: A knowledge panel is a box that appears in search results, usually on the right side, summarizing key facts about an entity like a person, company, or place, often pulled from a knowledge graph. Appearing accurately in one depends heavily on having clear, consistent entity information across the web.

topics.title: Lexical vs Vector Search
topics.description: Lexical search matches the literal words in a query against the literal words in a document, similar to a find-and-replace function. Vector search instead converts text into numerical representations and matches based on meaning, so it can find relevant content even when no exact words overlap. Most modern retrieval systems, including those used by AI models, combine both methods rather than relying on just one.
resources: Vector Databases vs Lexical Models in AI Search
What Is Vector Search? Difference Between Vector & Semantic Search Explained
Lexical Search vs Semantic Search. What's the difference?

topics.title: Link Building
topics.description: Link building is the practice of getting other websites to link to your own. Search engines treat links from other sites as a signal of trust and authority, so a page with many relevant, high-quality links pointing to it is generally treated as more credible than one with none.

topics.title: Link Schemes
topics.description: A link scheme is any pattern of link building designed to manipulate rankings rather than earned through genuine editorial merit, such as buying links, excessive link exchanges, or using automated programs to generate links at scale. Search engines explicitly prohibit these practices and can penalize sites found participating in them.
resources: What Is a Link Scheme in SEO? How Google Detects It
Combating Link Spam - Intro to Computer Science

topics.title: LLM Referral Traffic
topics.description: LLM referral traffic is website visits that originate specifically from a link clicked inside an AI chat assistant's response, such as a source cited by ChatGPT or Perplexity. Tracking it separately from other referral traffic shows how much real, measurable value AI visibility is actually generating.

topics.title: Local Citations
topics.description: A local citation is a mention of a business's name, address, and phone number on another website or directory, even without a clickable link. Citations act as independent confirmations of a business's legitimacy and location, similar to how backlinks confirm a website's authority.

topics.title: Local Landing Pages
topics.description: Local landing pages are dedicated pages for each location or service area a business serves, containing details specific to that place such as address, opening hours, services offered, local reviews, and an embedded map. They work best when each page has genuinely unique content rather than a template with only the city name swapped, which risks being treated as thin or duplicate content.
resources: Local Landing Pages: How to Build Pages That Rank and Convert for Every Location
Local Landing Pages: The Complete SEO Guide

topics.title: Local Links
topics.description: Local links are backlinks from other websites that are relevant to a specific geographic area, such as local news outlets, local business associations, or local bloggers. They typically carry more weight for local rankings than a generic link from an unrelated site with no local connection.

topics.title: Local Pack & Maps
topics.description: The Local Pack is the block of three business listings, shown alongside a map, that appears at the top of Google's results for local searches such as "coffee shop near me." Appearing in this block depends on a combination of Google Business Profile completeness, reviews, and local relevance.

topics.title: Local Search
topics.description: Local search covers the baseline setup required to appear in local search results, before rankings can meaningfully improve. This includes claiming and completing a Google Business Profile, keeping business details consistent everywhere they appear, gathering citations from other sites, and building dedicated pages for each location or service area served.

topics.title: Log File Analysis
topics.description: Log file analysis is examining a website's raw server logs to see exactly how search engine crawlers are behaving, including which pages they visit, how often, and which ones they ignore. It gives a more accurate picture of actual crawler behavior than simulated crawls from third-party tools, since it reflects what really happened rather than what should happen.
resources: Log file analysis for SEO: Find crawl issues & fix them fast
Server Log Analysis | Find and Fix SEO Errors

topics.title: Machine-Readable Content
topics.description: Machine-readable content is content structured in a way that a computer program can parse cleanly, rather than requiring visual interpretation the way a human reader would. This means using proper HTML structure, avoiding critical information hidden inside images or scripts, and keeping text in a form crawlers and AI systems can extract directly.
resources: The Content Manager’s Guide to Machine-Readable Content
SEO content: A complete guide for search and AI
AI-Readable SEO: How To Build A Machine-Readable Brand
From SEO to AEO: Is your PDP Machine Readable?

topics.title: Majestic
topics.description: Majestic is a backlink analysis tool best known for producing the Trust Flow and Citation Flow metrics, which estimate the quality and quantity of links pointing to a website.

topics.title: Managing AI Crawlers
topics.description: Managing AI crawlers involves controlling how automated bots and large language model scrapers access and process the content on your website. This practice allows you to balance visibility for traditional search engines while maintaining control over how your proprietary data is consumed and utilized by emerging artificial intelligence technologies.
resources: AI Crawlers: The List of AI Bots & How to Control Them

topics.title: Manual Actions & Recovery
topics.description: A manual action is a penalty applied directly by a human reviewer at a search engine, usually for violating guidelines, which can significantly reduce or remove a site's visibility. Recovery means identifying and fixing the underlying issue, then submitting a reconsideration request asking the search engine to review and lift the penalty.
resources: Manual Actions report in Search Console - Google Search Console Training

topics.title: MarketMuse
topics.description: MarketMuse is a content planning and optimization tool that uses AI to identify content gaps within a topic, suggesting what related subjects a site should cover to be seen as comprehensive on that subject.

topics.title: MCP & Structured Access
topics.description: MCP, or Model Context Protocol, is a standard that lets AI systems connect to external tools and data sources in a structured, predictable way, rather than only reading unstructured web pages. Structured access through protocols like this can give AI agents more reliable, direct access to a website's data than scraping its rendered HTML.

topics.title: Meta Descriptions
topics.description: A meta description is a short summary in a page's HTML that search engines often display below the title in search results. It does not directly affect rankings, but a compelling meta description can improve click-through rate by giving searchers a clear reason to choose that result.
resources: Best practices for creating quality meta descriptions
What Is a Meta Description? (+ Examples & Tips)
How To Write Perfect* Page Titles and Meta Descriptions for SEO
How Google Wants You to Create Meta Descriptions

topics.title: Microsoft Clarity
topics.description: Microsoft Clarity is a free analytics tool that provides heatmaps and session recordings, showing how visitors actually move through and interact with a page, rather than just reporting traffic numbers.

topics.title: Mobile Friendliness
topics.description: Mobile friendliness is whether a website works properly on a phone screen, including readable text, tappable buttons, and no horizontal scrolling. Most search engines evaluate a site primarily by its mobile version rather than its desktop version, since most searches happen on mobile devices.
resources: The Complete Guide to Mobile SEO: 9 Tips & Best Practices
How to Make Your Site Mobile Friendly for SEO

topics.title: Multi-Location SEO
topics.description: Multi-location SEO covers strategies specific to businesses with more than one physical location, or businesses that serve a defined area without a fixed storefront, such as a mobile repair service. These businesses need dedicated pages and listings for each location or service area, rather than treating the business as a single generic entity.

topics.title: Multi-Step AI Intent
topics.description: Multi-step AI intent describes how a single user question can require several rounds of reasoning and retrieval before an AI system produces a final answer, rather than one direct lookup. The system may retrieve information, evaluate whether it answers part of the question, then retrieve again to fill remaining gaps. This behavior is common in conversational and agentic AI systems handling complex questions.
resources: What Is Multi-Step Reasoning in AI Agents
Multi-step AI agents: what they are & how they work
Build an AI Agent that Adapts to User Intent

topics.title: NAP Consistency
topics.description: NAP stands for Name, Address, and Phone number. NAP consistency means keeping these three details identical across every website and directory where a business appears, since inconsistencies, such as "St." in one place and "Street" in another, can confuse systems trying to confirm it is the same business.

topics.title: News & Discovery SEO
topics.description: News and Discovery SEO is about earning visibility in Google surfaces that recommend content without a typed query, such as Top Stories, Google News, and the Discover feed. These surfaces favor fresh, original, well-sourced content with clear authorship and publish dates, high-quality images, and headlines that describe the story accurately rather than relying on clickbait.
resources: News SEO basics guide for publishers
How to Rank a News Website in Google: 9 Proven Strategies for 2026
Unlock Google Discover for Unlimited Traffic in 2026 🚀

topics.title: Niche Forums
topics.description: Niche forums are smaller, topic-specific online communities focused on a particular industry, hobby, or interest, as opposed to large general platforms. They often contain highly specific, candid discussion that both search and AI systems draw on when answering detailed questions within that niche.

topics.title: Nofollow, Noindex, and Disallow
topics.description: Nofollow, noindex, and disallow are instructions used to manage how search engines interact with your website. A "nofollow" tag tells search engines not to pass authority to a specific link, a "noindex" meta tag prevents a page from appearing in search results, and a "disallow" command in a robots.txt file instructs search engine crawlers to avoid scanning certain parts of your site entirely. These tools give you control over which pages are indexed and how crawling resources are allocated across your domain.
resources: Noindex vs. Nofollow vs. Disallow: When to Use Each One
Tech SEO: What is the difference between Noindex, Nofollow, and Disallow?

topics.title: Nofollow, Sponsored, UGC
topics.description: The nofollow attribute tells search engines not to pass ranking credit through a link. The sponsored attribute specifically marks a link as paid or part of an advertising arrangement. The UGC, or user-generated content, attribute marks links found in content like comments or forum posts, which a site owner did not personally place or endorse.

topics.title: On-Page SEO
topics.description: On-page SEO is the practice of optimizing individual web pages to improve their search engine rankings and earn more relevant traffic. It involves refining both the content and the HTML source code of a page, such as optimizing titles, headings, meta descriptions, and internal links.
resources: What Is On-Page SEO? And How to Do It
What Is On-Page SEO? How To Optimize A Page
What is On-Page SEO - 2.1. SEO Course by Ahrefs
What Is On-Page SEO? Everything You Need to Know In 2025

topics.title: Organization & Person Schema
topics.description: Organization schema and Person schema are structured data types used to explicitly identify a company or an individual on a web page. They can include details like name, logo, job title, or affiliation, giving search and AI systems clear, structured facts rather than requiring them to infer this from unstructured text.

topics.title: Organic vs Paid vs Direct
topics.description: Organic traffic comes from unpaid search results. Paid traffic comes from search ads, marked separately from organic results. Direct traffic is when someone reaches a website by typing the URL directly or using a saved bookmark, without going through a search engine at all. Separating these traffic types is essential for understanding where visitors are actually coming from.
resources: The Differences Between Paid And Organic Content On Social Media
Paid, organic and direct – What’s the difference?
Organic VS Paid Marketing Search Strategies The Pros and Cons | Neil Patel

topics.title: Original Research & Surveys
topics.description: This means running your own study or survey instead of citing research that someone else already conducted. It produces original data that did not exist before, giving other sources, including AI systems, a reason to cite your content specifically as the origin.
resources: How to Use Original Research to Boost Your International SEO Efforts
How surveys can improve your SEO and content strategy

topics.title: Otterly
topics.description: Otterly is a tool that monitors brand visibility and citations within AI search and chat platforms, tracking how often a brand appears and in what context.

topics.title: Page Authority
topics.description: Page Authority is a Moz metric similar to Domain Authority, but measured for a single page instead of an entire website. It estimates how likely that specific page is to rank well, based on the links pointing directly to it.

topics.title: PageSpeed Insights
topics.description: PageSpeed Insights is a free tool from Google that measures a page's loading speed and reports its Core Web Vitals scores. It gives specific, actionable suggestions for improving performance, such as compressing images or reducing unused code.

topics.title: Pagination
topics.description: Pagination is when content is split across multiple linked pages, such as page 1, page 2, and page 3 of a product listing. Handling it correctly means signaling to search engines that these pages are part of one continuous sequence, rather than unrelated content competing with each other.
resources: Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search
Pagination and SEO: A Complete Guide to Best Practices
Every Smart SEO Uses This Pagination Strategy

topics.title: Peec AI
topics.description: Peec is a platform for tracking a brand's presence and share of voice within AI-generated answers, comparing performance against competitors across a defined set of prompts.

topics.title: People Also Ask
topics.description: People Also Ask is a feature in Google search results showing a list of related questions that expand to reveal short answers when clicked. It is a useful source of real, common questions people have around a topic, and getting featured in it can drive visibility even without a top-ranking position.
resources: People Also Ask: What It Is & How to Optimize for It
The 5-Minute SEO Hack: Turn ‘People Also Ask’ Into Instant Topical Authority
The ‘People Also Ask’ SEO Hack That Builds Authority & Drives Sales

topics.title: Perplexity
topics.description: Perplexity is an AI-powered search product built specifically to answer questions directly, retrieving information from the web and presenting a synthesized response with citations, rather than showing a traditional list of links to click through.

topics.title: PerplexityBot
topics.description: PerplexityBot is the crawler operated by Perplexity, used to gather live web content when generating answers for its AI-powered search product. It can be allowed or blocked through a site's robots.txt file, similar to other AI crawlers.
resources: What is PerplexityBot? How to Optimize Your Site for AI Citations in 2026
PerplexityBot: What It Is, How It Works, and Why Every SEO Needs to Know

topics.title: Personalization & Localization
topics.description: Personalization is when search results differ based on an individual user's history, preferences, or device. Localization is when results differ based on geographic location, showing nearby businesses or region-specific content. Both mean that search results are not a single fixed list, but vary depending on who is searching and from where.

topics.title: Pitchbox
topics.description: Pitchbox is an outreach automation platform used for link building and digital PR, helping teams find contacts, send templated pitches, and manage follow-ups across large outreach campaigns.

topics.title: Planning & Checklists
topics.description: This is the preparation phase of a site migration, involving documenting the current site's structure, deciding what will change, and building a checklist to make sure nothing gets missed during the transition.
resources: A 6-step guide to building a website migration plan

topics.title: Position & Share of Search
topics.description: Average position is where a page typically ranks for a given query. Share of search measures what percentage of all search interest in a category or topic a brand is actually capturing, which gives a broader view of visibility than tracking individual keyword rankings alone.

topics.title: Post-Migration Monitoring
topics.description: Post-migration monitoring is closely tracking a website's rankings, traffic, and crawl behavior in the period immediately following a migration, to catch and fix problems quickly before they cause lasting damage.
resources: Post-Migration SEO Audit: Checklist for Traffic Recovery
Post-Migration Monitoring for 6 Months: The Week-by-Week Plan to Protect a Domain Migration’s SEOPost-Migration Monitoring for 6 Months: The Week-by-Week Plan to Protect a Domain Migration’s SEO

topics.title: Preferred Sources
topics.description: Preferred sources are the specific websites and publications that a given AI system consistently favors when choosing what to cite, often shaped by factors like established authority, structured content, or crawl accessibility. Identifying which sources an AI system prefers within a given topic helps inform where content or PR efforts might be most effective.

topics.title: Primary Data & Visuals
topics.description: Primary data and visuals encompass original research, proprietary data, or custom-made images and charts, rather than reused stock content or numbers pulled from someone else's report. This is one of the strongest ways to demonstrate information gain, since original material cannot be found anywhere else.

topics.title: Product & Place Schema
topics.description: Product schema and Place schema are structured data types used to explicitly describe a product, such as its price and availability, or a physical location, such as a business address and hours. They let search engines display rich details directly in results and give AI systems clear, structured facts to draw from.

topics.title: Profound
topics.description: Profound is a platform built specifically to track how often and how favorably a brand appears within AI-generated answers across different AI systems.

topics.title: Prompt Coverage & Mentions
topics.description: Prompt coverage measures how often a brand appears across a representative set of prompts within its category, when tested against AI systems. Mention rate is the frequency of those appearances, whether or not the brand is directly cited as a source.

topics.title: Proprietary Datasets
topics.description: A proprietary dataset is information only you have access to, such as internal usage data, customer behavior, or transaction data, that a competitor cannot easily replicate. Publishing insights drawn from it gives content a form of information gain that is difficult for others to copy.
resources: The SEO Advantage of Proprietary Data (And Why Google Rewards It)
Why Proprietary Research Data Is Key to Brand Differentiation

topics.title: Pruning & Deindexing
topics.description: Pruning is the practice of removing or merging low-performing, outdated, or thin content from a website rather than letting it accumulate indefinitely. Deindexing is the technical step of formally telling search engines to remove a page from their index, typically done once that content has been pruned or is no longer meant to be found in search.

topics.title: Query & Topic Coverage
topics.description: Query coverage is how many relevant search queries a site actually appears for, out of all the queries related to its topic. Topic coverage looks at this at a broader level, checking whether a site comprehensively addresses a subject or only touches a small part of it.

topics.title: Query Fan-Out
topics.description: Query fan-out is when an AI system breaks a single user question into several smaller sub-questions before retrieving information to answer it. A question like "best CRM for a small SaaS company" might get split internally into separate queries about pricing, integrations, and reviews. This means content can get retrieved for the pieces of an answer, not just for the exact phrase someone typed.
resources: What is query fan-out? How to find & optimize for subqueries
The Query-Fan Out AI SEO System is INSANE
How to Use Query Fan-Out To Rank Content FAST in AI Search

topics.title: Question Mining
topics.description: Question mining is the practice of finding the actual questions real people ask about a topic, then using those questions as the basis for content. It draws on sources where people ask things directly, rather than relying only on keyword tools that show search phrases without context.
resources: Question Mining for AI Search in 2026
The queries your competitors can't see
Find the questions people also asked
How to Find Questions Around Your Top SEO Keywords

topics.title: RAG
topics.description: RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It is a method where an AI system first retrieves relevant documents or passages from an external source, then uses that retrieved content to generate its answer, rather than relying only on what it learned during training. This is the mechanism behind how many AI systems produce answers that cite or reflect current web content.
resources: What is retrieval augmented generation (RAG)? - IBM

topics.title: Rank Tracking
topics.description: Rank tracking is the practice of monitoring where a website ranks for specific target keywords over time, using dedicated tools that check search results regularly.

topics.title: Redirect Chains & Loops
topics.description: A redirect chain is a sequence of multiple redirects in a row before reaching the final destination page, which slows down loading and wastes crawl budget. A redirect loop is when a chain of redirects eventually points back to an earlier page in the sequence, creating an endless cycle that prevents the page from ever loading.
resources: Redirect chains: How they waste crawl budget and break rendering
How to Locate and Fix Redirect Loops

topics.title: Redirect Mapping
topics.description: Redirect mapping is the process of creating a complete list matching every old URL to its correct new destination during a site migration. Missing or incorrect mappings can cause pages to lose their rankings entirely, since search engines may treat an unmapped old URL as simply gone rather than moved.
resources: Complete redirect mapping guide for website migrations
Manage redirects during a website migration: What works
301 Redirects: The Ultimate Guide To Website Migration (SEO)

topics.title: Rendering & JavaScript SEO
topics.description: Some websites build their content using JavaScript that runs in the browser, instead of sending fully formed HTML. If a crawler cannot execute that JavaScript properly, it may see a blank or incomplete page instead of the finished content. This node covers making sure what a crawler receives actually matches what a real visitor sees.

topics.title: Retrieval vs Ranking
topics.description: Retrieval is the step where a search or AI system pulls a set of candidate documents that might answer a query, based on relevance matching. Ranking is a separate step that follows, ordering those retrieved candidates from most to least relevant. A page can be successfully retrieved as a candidate and still rank poorly, or fail to be retrieved at all regardless of how well it would rank if found.
resources: Google Ranking vs AI Retrieval: Why #1 Isn't Enough
A guide to Google Search ranking systems

topics.title: Reviews & Velocity
topics.description: Review velocity is how steadily new customer reviews come in over time, not just the overall star rating. A business that suddenly receives many reviews in a single day can look suspicious to review platforms, while a steady, ongoing flow of reviews looks organic and healthy.

topics.title: Robots.txt
topics.description: Robots.txt is a text file placed at the root of a website that tells crawlers which parts of the site they are allowed or not allowed to visit. It can be used to block specific bots entirely, including AI crawlers, or to keep crawlers away from pages like admin panels or duplicate content. It works on trust, since well-behaved bots follow it but not all crawlers do.
resources: What Is A Robots.txt File? A Guide to Best Practices and Syntax
SEO Tutorial - The role of robots.txt files

topics.title: SameAs & Entity Linking
topics.description: The SameAs property in schema markup links a page's entity to that same entity's presence elsewhere on the web, such as its official social media profiles or Wikipedia page. This helps a system confirm that multiple different pages all refer to the same real-world entity.

topics.title: Scaled Content Abuse
topics.description: Scaled content abuse is producing large volumes of low-quality content, often with little to no human oversight, purely to manipulate search rankings rather than to genuinely help users. This has become a bigger focus for search engines as AI writing tools make it easier to generate content at scale without proportional quality.
resources: Scaled Content Abuse: Do's and Don'ts for SEO
Google’s War on Scaled AI Content: The Rise and Fall of AInvest

topics.title: Screaming Frog
topics.description: Screaming Frog is a desktop crawler tool that simulates how a search engine bot would crawl a website. It reports issues such as broken links, missing title tags, duplicate content, and pages blocked by robots.txt, and is one of the most widely used tools for technical SEO audits.
resources: Screaming Frog SEO Spider Tutorial - How To Do An SEO Audit

topics.title: Search Intent
topics.description: Search intent is the underlying goal behind a search query, such as wanting to buy something, learn something, or find a specific website. Two people can type different words but want the same thing, or type the same words and want different things. Matching content to the correct intent behind a query is often more important than matching the exact keyword.
resources: What Is Search Intent? How to Identify It & Optimize for It
What Is Search Intent and Why Does It Matter?
What is Search Intent in SEO, Explained!
Keyword Research Pt 1: How to Analyze Searcher Intent

topics.title: Semantic Search
topics.description: Semantic search is a method of finding relevant content based on meaning rather than exact keyword matches. It allows a system to understand that "cheap flights" and "affordable plane tickets" refer to the same idea. This is the foundation that lets modern search and AI systems retrieve relevant content even when the wording differs from the query.
resources: What is a Vector Database? Powering Semantic Search & AI Applications

topics.title: Semrush
topics.description: Semrush is an all-in-one SEO platform used for keyword research, rank tracking, competitor analysis, and backlink auditing. It also offers a dedicated AI Visibility Toolkit for tracking how a brand appears within AI-generated answers.
resources: Getting Started with Semrush: A Tutorial for Navigating the Essentials

topics.title: Semrush
topics.description: Semrush is an all-in-one marketing software suite that provides tools for keyword research, competitor analysis, and position tracking. It allows users to monitor their search engine rankings across various devices and locations, offering detailed data on visibility trends and performance changes over time.

topics.title: SEO Audits
topics.description: An SEO audit is a structured review of a website's technical health, content quality, and backlink profile, identifying issues and opportunities across all of these areas at once. It is typically the first step in diagnosing why a site is underperforming or in establishing a baseline before starting new work.

topics.title: SERP Analysis
topics.description: SERP analysis is examining the actual search results page for a target keyword to understand what type of content currently ranks, what format it takes, and what features like snippets or panels appear alongside it. This informs decisions about what kind of content is likely to succeed for that specific query.
resources: What Is a SERP Analysis & How Can You Do One?
How to Do a Competitor SERP Analysis
How to Analyze SERP to Improve Your Rankings
How to do Google SERP analysis

topics.title: SERP Features
topics.description: SERP features are the non-standard elements that can appear on a search results page beyond the normal list of blue links, such as sitelinks, knowledge panels, or image packs. Appearing in these features can significantly change how much visibility and traffic a result receives compared to a standard listing.

topics.title: SERP, Index, Crawl
topics.description: A SERP, or Search Engine Results Page, is the page shown after someone runs a search. The index is the search engine's stored database of pages it has processed and can retrieve. A crawl is the act of a bot visiting and reading a page's content, which happens before that page can be added to the index.
resources: What Is a SERP? Search Engine Results Pages Explained
Crawling vs. Indexing — The Quick Summary for Busy Marketers
SEO Basics: Crawling, Indexing, and Ranking
What is a SERP? Search Engine Results Pages (SERPs) Explained For Beginners

topics.title: Site Hierarchy & Depth
topics.description: Site hierarchy is the structure of how pages relate to each other, from the homepage down through categories to individual pages. Depth refers to how many clicks it takes to reach a given page from the homepage. A flatter hierarchy, where important pages are just a few clicks away, is generally easier for crawlers to find and fully explore.
resources: Site architecture: Creating a website structure that ranks
What Is Website Architecture? (& How to Improve it for SEO)
What Is Page Depth in SEO?
WHY HIERARCHY IS SO IMPORTANT IN WEB DESIGN

topics.title: Site Migrations
topics.description: A site migration is any major change to a website's structure, domain, or platform, such as moving to a new domain, switching from HTTP to HTTPS, or redesigning the URL structure. Migrations carry significant risk of losing search visibility if not planned and executed carefully, since search engines need to correctly understand that old URLs have moved to new ones.
resources: The Complete Beginner’s Guide To SEO Website Migrations

topics.title: Site Reputation Abuse
topics.description: Site reputation abuse is when a third party publishes low-quality content on a reputable site's subdomain or section, attempting to exploit that site's existing authority and trust for their own ranking gain. Google has specifically targeted this practice, since it previously let unrelated, low-quality content unfairly benefit from a trusted domain's reputation.
resources: Understand Google's site reputation abuse policy: A guide for SEO leaders
Site Reputation Abuse: Is Your Website at Risk?
